{{Short description|Category whose objects are natural numbers and whose morphisms are matrices}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''category of matrices''', often denoted <math>\mathbf{Mat}</math>, is the [[category (category theory)|category]] whose [[object (category theory)|object]]s are [[natural number]]s and whose [[morphism]]s are [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]], with composition given by [[matrix multiplication]].<ref>{{harvp|Riehl|2016|pages=4-5}}</ref><ref name="perrone-matrix">{{harvp|Perrone|2024|pages=99-100}}</ref>

== Construction ==

Let <math>A</math> be an <math>n\times m</math> [[real number|real]] [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]], i.e. a matrix with <math>n</math> rows and <math>m</math> columns. 
Given a <math>p\times q</math> matrix <math>B</math>, we can form the [[matrix multiplication]] <math>BA</math> or <math>B\circ A</math> only when <math>q=n</math>, and in that case the resulting matrix is of dimension <math>p\times m</math>. 

In other words, we can only multiply matrices <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> when the number of rows of <math>A</math> matches the number of columns of <math>B</math>. 
One can keep track of this fact by declaring an <math>n\times m</math> matrix to be of type <math>m\to n</math>, and similarly a <math>p\times q</math> matrix to be of type <math>q\to p</math>. This way, when <math>q=n</math> the two arrows have matching source and target, <math>m\to n\to p</math>, and can hence be composed to an arrow of type <math>m\to p</math>.

This is precisely captured by the mathematical concept of a [[category (mathematics)|category]], where the arrows, or [[morphisms]], are the matrices, and they can be composed only when their domain and codomain are compatible (similar to what happens with [[function (mathematics)|functions]]). In detail, the category <math>\mathbf{Mat}_\mathbb{R}</math> is constructed as follows:

* It has [[natural numbers]] as [[object (category theory)|objects]];

* Given numbers <math>m</math> and <math>n</math>, a [[morphism]] <math>m\to n</math> is an <math>n\times m</math> matrix, i.e. a matrix with <math>n</math> rows and <math>m</math> columns;

* The [[identity morphism]] at each object <math>n</math> is given by the <math>n\times n</math> [[identity matrix]];

* The composition of morphisms <math>A:m\to n</math> and <math>B:n\to p</math> (i.e. of matrices <math>n\times m</math> and <math>p\times n</math>) is given by [[matrix multiplication]].

More generally, one can define the category <math>\mathbf{Mat}_\mathbb{F}</math> of matrices over a fixed field <math>\mathbb{F}</math>, such as the one of [[complex numbers]].

== Properties ==

* The category of matrices <math>\mathbf{Mat}_\mathbb{R}</math> is [[equivalence of categories|equivalent]] to the category of finite-dimensional real [[vector space]]s and [[linear map]]s. This is witnessed by the [[functor]] mapping the number <math>n</math> to the vector space <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>, and an <math>n\times m</math> matrix to the corresponding linear map <math>\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n</math>.<ref name="mat-eq">{{harvp|Riehl|2016|page=30}}</ref><ref name="perrone-matrix"/> A possible interpretation of this fact is that, as mathematical theories, abstract finite-dimensional vector spaces and concrete matrices have the same expressive power.

* More generally, the category of matrices <math>\mathbf{Mat}_\mathbb{F}</math> is [[equivalence of categories|equivalent]] to the category of finite-dimensional [[vector space]]s over the field <math>\mathbb{F}</math> and <math>\mathbb{F}</math>-[[linear map]]s.<ref name="mat-eq"/>

* A [[Matrix (mathematics)#Row operations|linear row operation]] on a <math>n\times m</math> matrix <math>A</math> can be equivalently obtained by applying the same operation to the <math>n\times n</math> [[identity matrix]], and then multiplying the resulting <math>n\times n</math> matrix with <math>A</math>. In particular, elementary row operations correspond to [[elementary matrices]]. This fact can be seen as an instance of the [[Yoneda lemma]] for the category of matrices.<ref>{{harvp|Riehl|2016|pages=60-61}}</ref><ref>{{harvp|Perrone|2024|pages=119-120}}</ref>

* The [[transpose]] operation makes the category of matrices a [[dagger category]]. The same can be said about the [[conjugate transpose]] in the case of [[complex number]]s.

== Particular subcategories ==

* For every fixed <math>n</math>, the morphisms <math>n\to n</math> of <math>\mathbf{Mat}_\mathbb{R}</math> are the <math>n\times n</math> matrices, and form a [[monoid]], canonically isomorphic to the monoid of linear endomorphisms of <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>. In particular, the [[invertible matrix|invertible]] <math>n\times n</math> matrices form a [[group (mathematics)|group]]. The same can be said for a generic field <math>\mathbb{F}</math>.

* A [[stochastic matrix]] is a real matrix of nonnegative entries, such that the sum of each column is one. Stochastic matrices include the identity and are closed under composition, and so they form a [[subcategory]] of <math>\mathbf{Mat}_\mathbb{R}</math>.<ref>{{harvp|Perrone|2024|pages=302-303}}</ref>
